title: Chapter 87 — The Referral and Review Engine
intro: Referrals and reviews are earned — not asked for. Build the system that generates them naturally.

sections.title: Referrals Come from Relationships
sections.content:
The best referrals happen without being asked. A customer has a friend who needs a new fridge. They say 'go see my person at the store.' That referral is more powerful than any advertisement because it comes with built-in trust.

You earn that by delivering exceptional experiences consistently. Follow the 10 Steps. Follow up after delivery. Stay connected through your cadence. When the referral comes, it is not because you asked — it is because you deserved it.

sections.title: Reviews Drive New Business
sections.content:
Online reviews are the modern version of word of mouth — except they reach thousands instead of a handful. A customer who leaves a five-star review describing their experience with you specifically is generating free marketing that no ad budget can buy.

The way to earn reviews is simple: deliver an experience worth writing about. Then make it easy. A follow-up message that says 'If you had a good experience, it would mean a lot if you left a review on Google' is enough. Most happy customers are willing — they just need the nudge.

sections.title: The Advocate Relationship
sections.content:
Some customers become advocates. They do not just buy from you and refer friends — they actively promote you. They talk about you at dinner parties. They recommend you on social media. They bring colleagues into the store.

You cannot manufacture advocates. But you can cultivate them by being consistently excellent, staying connected, and treating every interaction as an opportunity to reinforce the relationship.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating referral and review generation, ask:

Are referrals happening naturally — or not at all?
Does the salesperson ask for reviews in a genuine, non-pressured way?
Are they cultivating advocate relationships — or forgetting customers after the sale?
Is the review volume growing — or stagnant?

A strong referral and review engine compounds over time. It takes patience to build but pays dividends for years.
